faq.a1: Ducky collects company events, calculates technical and volatility indicators, and sends alerts based on your conditions. You can review the sources and historical results to inform your own decisions. It is a research tool, not personalized investment advice.
faq.a2: No. Ducky does not connect to brokerage accounts or place trades.
faq.q3: Can I use Ducky without Telegram?
faq.a3: Yes. New users can create a username and password with an invite. Existing users can sign in with a username or verified email. Telegram is an optional login and notification channel; supported browsers can also receive notifications.
faq.q4: How do I pay and cancel?
faq.a4: Choose a plan in Billing. Checkout lists the payment methods currently available. For fixed-term purchases, you can let the plan expire. If you use a recurring payment method, follow the cancellation instructions shown at checkout and on the order.
faq.q5: How often are data and alerts updated?
faq.a5: Update frequency varies by source, and pages show the data timestamp. Paid alerts are checked every 15 minutes during market hours. Source and service delays can affect delivery.
faq.a6: Signal records show price changes after 1, 5 and 20 trading days. Strategy backtests separately state their rules, costs and benchmarks. These are different measures. Losses and positions whose holding periods are not yet complete remain in the record.

footer.p1: Ducky TradeBot provides data, signals and educational tools for personal investment research. Nothing here is investment advice. Past performance does not predict future results. Consult a licensed financial adviser before making investment decisions.
footer.p2: Everything on this site and in the Telegram channel; insider buys, institutional stakes, the K-index, backtests, “receipt” screenshots; is a past-tense record of what an indicator or tool did, plus data education. It is not a stock pick, not an instruction to buy or sell, and carries no price targets and no promise of returns. We are not a licensed investment adviser with the CSRC or in any jurisdiction, and we do not offer advisory, managed-account, copy-trading or “insider list” services.
footer.p3: Ducky is not a trading bot: it connects to no brokerage account and never places an order. Every K-index push carries a stop-loss reminder; the backtest sample is limited and a historical “100%” does not predict the future. Paid tiers differ by personalization (watching your list), not by “secret picks”.
footer.p4: Personal trade entries document the author's research and trades and are not investment advice.
footer.backtest_line: Backtests are hypothetical. Each study states its trading cost assumptions; taxes are excluded.
footer.affiliation_line: Not affiliated with Telegram, the SEC, or any issuer named.

track.lead: Review signal dates and price changes after 1, 5 and 20 trading days, including losses. LIVE records were made at the time; BACKTEST entries are historical tests. Results are calculated separately.
track.rates_note: Hit = the return's sign matches the signal's direction. Every percentage carries its N=; rows with N below 20 are early readings, not conclusions.
track.equity_note: Positions begin at the signal base-date close: bullish messages are treated as long positions, bearish messages as shorts, and neutral messages as longs. Active positions’ daily returns are averaged and compounded; repeated messages can receive repeated weight. SPY is buy-and-hold over the same period. This legacy simulation is not a validated oversold strategy. All losses remain in the record. Fees, slippage, taxes and stock-borrow costs are excluded.

track.note_1: +1 / +5 / +20 = close on the 1st / 5th / 20th trading day after the signal vs. the signal-day close (%). Blank means the day hasn't arrived.
track.note_2: BACKTEST rows are historical replays; LIVE rows were actually pushed at the time. They are tallied separately and never mixed.
track.note_3: The ledger is archived nightly, with changes available in its history.

rev.curve_method_body: Positions begin at the signal base-date close: bullish messages are treated as long positions, bearish messages as shorts, and neutral messages as longs. Active positions’ daily returns are averaged and compounded; repeated messages can receive repeated weight. SPY is buy-and-hold over the same period. This legacy simulation is not a validated oversold strategy. All losses remain in the record.
os.title: What happens after an oversold recovery?
os.intro: Enter at the next open after an oversold recovery above the 5-day average. Equal stock weights, held for 20 sessions.
os.chart: Backtested oversold portfolio versus SPY and QQQ
os.risk_body: In 2022, the portfolio returned {nav}%, versus {spy}% for SPY and {qqq}% for QQQ. Maximum drawdown in the charted period was {dd}%.
os.method_body: The rule was selected from three fixed rules using 2019-2021 returns, then evaluated separately in 2022 and from 2023 onward. Each period starts in cash. Stock weights reset equally at each open; idle cash earns no interest and open positions are marked at the close.
os.limitations: Retrospective research using a universe selected today, with selection and survivorship bias. Historical IV/HV, fundamentals and option walls are not included. This is a price-only baseline, not live performance or validation of the complete strategy. All triggered positions and losses are retained.

os.rule_detail: Trigger: daily RSI(14) ≤35 and a drawdown of at least 15% from the 252-session high on a day within the prior ten sessions, followed by a close crossing above the 5-session average. Act only when the rule switches from false to true.
